chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Maskan, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I was with Ziyad ibn Abdillah, and Rabee'at al-Ra'y was with him. Ziyad said to him: 'O Rabee', what did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declare forbidden in Medina?' He said to him: 'Mail for mail.' I said to Rabee': 'Was there mail during the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family)?' He became silent and did not answer me. Ziyad turned to me and said: 'O Abu Abdillah, then what do you say?' I said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declared forbidden in Medina, from the game, that which is between the two Labas.' He said: 'And what are their two Labas?' I said: 'That which is surrounded by the heat (climate/region).' He said to me: 'What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declare forbidden from trees?' I said: 'From 'Eer to Wa'er.'

Safwan said: Ibn Maskan said: Hasan said: Then a person asked him while I was sitting, and he said to him: 'And what are their two Labas?' He said: 'That which is between the two Suroon until the Thaniyyah.'

key_terms.الثَّنِيَّةُ: The Thaniyyah, a narrow mountain pass or road used as a boundary marker
key_terms.الصُّورَيْنِ: The two Suroon, specific landmarks or hills used to define the boundary
key_terms.الْحَرَارُ: The heat/climate, referring to the climatic region surrounding the city
key_terms.عِيرٍ إِلَى وَعِيرٍ: From 'Eer to Wa'er, a phrase indicating a specific extent or range of trees
key_terms.لَابَتَاهَا: The two Labas, a term used to define the boundary limits of the Haram of Medina

ai.seo_question: What are the boundaries of the Haram of Medina where hunting is forbidden?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar* elucidates the precise geographical limits of the Haram of Medina, resolving scholarly debates by defining the 'two Labas' either climatically or via specific topographical landmarks like the Suroon hills. It highlights the Imam’s method of clarifying ambiguous terms through both environmental and physical markers, reinforcing the sanctity of the city's boundaries for hunting prohibitions. This clarification underscores the importance of precise juristic definitions in maintaining the spiritual and legal integrity of sacred spaces.
